title: Better Than 4 Stars, but not Quite 5
review_text: Okay let's start with how my Mini Fridge arrived. Like all Refrigerators they arrive in an almost open ended box. The fridge sits on a base, then it's covered with a bottomless box & strapped in tightly. Because of this setup my Retro Fridge arrived damaged in 2 different places, it was missing this little plastic piece on the bottom that helps balance the fridge & the cord was forced into the opening on the back, which was extremely difficult to get out without damaging the mechanisms of the fridge. Aside from that, this is a really nice product & we love its functionality. The size is great, both the sections are very spacious for this little guy. It has great features just like a full size fridge. Multiple types of holders on the door, including several for drinks, butter, etc. The main area has 3 shelves inside & a veggie draw. The freezer is spacious as well with 2 separate shelves & ice cube tray. Now when setting up your fridge please be patient & follow directions carefully. You want to take your time allowing the fridge to come to temperature before loading it with food. Pay close attention to the temperature after you begin adding food, so that you can get the temperature right for what you're adding. That being said don't load the fridge with food to quickly, add small amounts at a time so that you don't over work the motor. If you can try to add some items that are already cold or frozen, this will assist your little guy in getting cold easier. After you've found what works for you, be sure to pay attention to both top & bottom sections. Ice will form in the back of the fridge area as well, it's because the freezer is not self defrosting. You'll need to scrape you freezer about every 3 months, but I'd do it a little quicker for better life on your purchase. There's a small hole in the back of the fridge section for water draining, it makes a little noise once in a while but that's completely normal. I'd definitely Recommend this product, with proper care it should last you for years. Thanks

The Bluetooth music quality was definitely better than I was expecting for an emergency radio though, and the Seek and Play buttons double as the Bluetooth track controls. Sadly you can't set presets for the Weather Mode, but there are 22 presets for the Radio, which can be set and cycled through easily. The flashlight has 3 modes, High, Low, and flashing which is nice. I love that the Alert function works in all modes including Standby mode if you want. The reception is okay, FM definitely worked better than NOAA in my area though. Finally, you can't use the charging USB port when it's switched to using the backup AA Batteries which really stinks considering the small internal battery, and the USB charging port is only 1A, which means nothing will charge quickly either. Conclusion - The small 2500mAh internal battery, the lack of AA battery to USB charging capability, and the 1A charging port make this hard to recommend. But if you only need a basic emergency alert radio, not a full blown backup battery pack too, this will suffice.

I have owned a set of these tires before on a 2000 Saturn LS1 in size 205-60R-15. Most of my driving experience with these come from that vehicle. After owning a set of Michelin Premier A/S for the last two years, I chose to switch back to the Goodyear Assurance Fuel Max tires. Consumer Reports ranks the Goodyear tires lower than the top rated Michelins. However, in my experience, I feel that the Goodyear is truer to it's performance promise. For every day driving, most drivers will find that the Goodyear assurance delivers better than expected performance for a tire whose primary mission is fuel economy. With a good suspension set up, the tires will grip well in the dry, allowing the driver to handle long sweeper curves at 10-20 mph faster than the posted speed without feeling overburdened. They also provide plenty of audible warning when the traction limit is getting close. The downside is the wet weather traction. Especially in light rain for the first 1/2 hour when the roads can still be very slick. Be especially careful with these tires approaching intersections and stop signs as these areas tend to have collected grease patches on the ground from previous cars. Many times, without paying my full attention I have activated the Anti-lock brakes with only moderate braking force. This has caused me to "stop long" and overshoot the intersection. Thankfully, no other cross traffic was approaching and I was able to throw the car into reverse. But one users minor embarrassment could be another user's fatal accident. If you buy these tires, be extremely cautious in the wet. The surprise upside to these tires is the snow traction. Several times, during the winter, my car had been parked on the street and 'plowed in'. Most car owners spend 1/2 hour shoveling out their cars and spinning their tires in the process. I have to say that as long as these tires had passable tread on them, I never had to excessively rock my car back and forth or have anyone help push me out of a driveway apron or other snowy situation. Even driving 30mph on a snowy highway (about 5" of snow) that had other vehicles fish tailing (some were even Subaru's!), my car was stable. Don't get me wrong, I activated the traction control system many times with these all-seasons in the snow and a true winter tire would blow them away. But if you are someone who doesn't have the luxury of being able to store a separate set of winter tires, like me, the winter traction of these tires are better-than-expected. The ride quality falls somewhere between sporty and flinty. They can absorb a decent amount of rough pavement. But if you live in an area with seriously neglected roads, you will notice that these tires aren't a luxury tire after-all. Road noise is very good and these tires only really started developing a warbling-humming noise when they were near the end of their life. Speaking of which, the tread life is also very good. I believe that Goodyear has a 60k mile tread-life rating. I got about 55K out of them. I am very careful to check tire pressure and get an alignment at least 1x per year and I try to rotate the tires every 5000-8000 miles. Oh, and the low rolling resistance/Fuel-Economy claim is legit. I averaged about 0.5 to 1mpg (it is more noticeable on the highway, but if you know how to time city traffic lights and coast in gear you can improve city mileage as well) better than I usually got with my Michelin Premier A/S tires. The Michelin's did have a cushier ride and they handled the wet conditions masterfully. However, their snow traction felt very 'greasy' and I got stuck a couple of times in snow less than 3" thick. Overall, if you are consciously aware of the wet traction warning with these tires, the combination of sporty ride, tread-life and fuel economy will deliver value. And as an added bonus, they are pretty good in the snow, as far as all-seasons are concerned.

I had read reviews saying the tires are loud, but they seem quieter than my previous tires. I hope that continues. My old Michelin tires were supposedly energy saving tires, too. I am not getting any improvement in gas mileage after 4 or 5 fill-ups with the Goodyears. In fact I would say my gas mileage has gotten worse by a MPG or so. I am hoping these tires are as long-wearing as the Michelins were. If not, I would consider them a bad trade.

I asked the staff if they could call the next closest Walmart Auto Center to see if they could install them. We waited for 20 minutes on hold and finally were informed that they had the proper lift, lift was in working order, and they had time to install them. It took me 8 minutes to drive there, waited 20 minutes to have someone check me in, was told that it would be about an hour and that they would text me. After an hour and a half, I went back to the auto center to see if they were about done and noticed that my car was still in the original place I parked it. I asked a staff member how much longer it would be and they told me that they couldn't to it because the lift they needed wasn't working. They suggested that I take my tires and go to Firestone for installation. Although they refunded my installation fees, I went to Discount Tire for installation which costed me double what I was refunded since I didn't buy the tires from them, but they had them installed in about 30 minutes. I would recommend the tires but would not recommend Walmart Auto Centers in Wetumpka or Pratville, AL.

title: starter tool kit
review_text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I received this item for free in exchange for my honest review. The Hyper tough 70 piece project kit comes with a cordless drill, battery, charger, some basic tools and driver bits. It seems fine. For a small handheld drill, it did the job as I was drilling some holes in pvc. The torque seemed fine for this sized drill. It's not going to do much more than basic household projects. It's not as heavy as some of the other drills I've owned, and it feels pretty well-balanced with the battery connected. The other tools also seem to be in the "fine" category. You aren't going to be framing anything with the hammer but if you need to hang a picture it'll work. The needle nose pliers didn't quite cut the wire I tried, the blades need some filing. It however does close with some decent force at the plier end. The tape measure housing is cheap plastic, but seems accurate in measurements. A really nice addition that this comes with is a ratcheting screwdriver. Soap box time: Calling a tool set "70 piece" when 60 of those pieces are driver bits kind of drives me crazy. It's not like it came with 70 tools, yes there are 70 pieces (including the carry case) but it always seems misleading to me for some reason. The battery charger. It works, it's fine. I've seen this a lot in cordless drills and it always ends up being a failure point. The wire between the wall adapter and the charging block is 24 awg. It's very thin. It doesn't need to be thick for the electrical properties, but it will be the first thing to break. When you go to fix it, stripping and splicing that thin a wire can be difficult. I wish manufacturers would at least put 20 awg on it. When it breaks, which it will with even normal wear and tear, you're not going to be able to fix it as they just want you to buy another 70 piece project kit. That being said, this would be something you'd give to your niece as she moves into her first apartment in college.
